posts.title: That time I tried to use ChatGPT to write The Expanse: The Musical
posts.tagline: Or, the story of how five characters all high-fived each other at the same time.
posts.summary: If we've ever spoken about the pitfalls of AI, you may have heard me reference the "collective high-five:" a somewhat tongue-in-cheek phrase I coined to characterize the "training wheels" that safeguard users from the darker potentials of LLMs. The "high-five" means that everything works out for everyone in the end; it's the silver lining, or maybe the toxic positivity sometimes found on your social media feed. posts.content:
If we've ever spoken about the pitfalls of AI, you may have heard me reference the "collective high-five:" a somewhat tongue-in-cheek phrase I coined to characterize the "training wheels" that safeguard users from the darker potentials of LLMs.

The "high-five" means that everything works out for everyone in the end; it's the silver lining, or maybe the toxic positivity sometimes found on your social media feed. Today, I invite you on a quick ChatGPT-generated journey through space—to laugh along with me—as we try to generate "The Expanse: The Musical (Unlicensed!)", based on the hit novel and TV series by James S. A. Corey (authors Daniel Abraham and Ty Franck).

Caution: spoilers ahead, read at your own peril!

The Idea

Near the beginning of ChatGPT 3.5's release to the world, I wanted to test its creative limits. Maybe ChatGPT would be the writing buddy I'd always wanted. I also wanted to know: did it have a sense of humor? What could ChatGPT write, and where did it fall short? Of course, the best way to test this was to generate a hit Broadway musical. I blithely started a new chat:

Great! Pretty accurate.

The Music

Now it was time to write the songs. At first, ChatGPT wowed me: these were no less cheesy than lyrics from the likes of Frank Wildhorn (sorry, Frank).

We even wrote a sad song for some interpersonal conflict (where the first cracks began to show: if you know the series, you know these characters aren't actually in love). It was also around this time I began to notice that while the songs didn't always have the same rhyming scheme, the composition was noticeably simple. Ah well, minor details, and I was having too much fun by this point.

Already, some themes had begun to emerge in ChatGPT's writing: notably, the idea of striving together toward a common purpose, overcoming odds, etc. Empowering! I think?

The comic relief, in this endless night

Usually when I tell people this story, this is the point where I make fun of ChatGPT for inventing the ridiculous character we're about to meet. But in writing this, I've remembered that I was the one who asked it to add a “comic relief character,” so I guess the blame lies partially with me. Ever the chipper collaborator, it came up with some songs by new original character Bobby the Belter:

(But of course, we were missing a primary Belter characteristic, so I added some coaching to get it to include the Belter creole:)

As we all know, the main thing that makes a comic relief character funny is their tendency to go around talking about how they're the comic relief...

By the way, the AI decided to cast Danny Trejo in the role, whom I personally think is a great fit:

Pushing the Boundaries, apparently

At this point I thought it would be fun to inject some puns into the writing, but ChatGPT was not in favor of this unfortunately:

Thankfully we were able to reach a common understanding with “wholesome wordplay” - from there, it was time to get to writing some actual scenes (but not about the Protomolecule apparently):

The irony of an AI saying this was perhaps the funniest thing of all. Of course, there are folks out there attempting to use AI ethically (and here I am having fun with a LLM populated with content cribbed from everywhere across the entire internet). But the Protomolecule, for those unfamiliar, is an AI, originally developed to help conquer the universe, which has developed sentience and laid waste to entire civilations.

Now why on earth would ChatGPt not want to write about that?

The Famous High-Five

Anyway, by this point, we were writing full-on scenes (and I've left probably hours of conversation out since this is already getting long). So I will leave you with the sequence that led to the magnum opus, the point of this entire post:

And isn't that just how everything works out in real life, in the end? Everyone laughing and continuing their work, while the stage lights fade to black?

But it had started to feel like we were straying a little far from the source material and themes of the series. I mean, some of these characters have lived their entire lives in space. It should be mundane to them...

Alright, this is... closer! We're getting somewhere. Bobby the Belter has somehow morphed into Gunnery Sergeant Bobbie Draper (played wonderfully by Frankie Adams, who is, as you will observe, factually not the same person as Danny Trejo).

At least we're not talking about the singular topic of hope and excitement about the future, against all odds. Maybe we'll actually get to explore some of the rich, dense thematic offerings of the original authors...

And there you have it: the point where I simply gave up, the high-five between five characters all at the same time.

I will leave you to draw your own conclusions.

Disclaimer

Of course LLMs are not all safeguarded like this, and all this was early ChatGPT 3.5, anyway. "You're stupid about AI," you may be thinking. "You didn't put any effort into actually poking holes in the writing capabilities of AI. This was a waste of time!"

But wasn't it fun?! Isn't that what life's all about—fun? Hey, I know! What if we add some excitement to space?

High-five.

Also, I do not in any way claim to own the rights to The Expanse or The Expanse: The Musical. But Ty Franck, let me know if you'd like to talk...
